_what: How harness/work-consumer.mjs starts each desktop AI host on work handed to it. One row per host: `check` is a command that proves the host's documented interface is installed; `wake` is the host's own command that starts a turn in the named existing session (argv, with {session} and {message} filled in), or `channel: true` for a host that runs this consumer itself as its channel server and is told over stdio, with `protocol_versions` the MCP revisions its handshake may answer (the first when the host asks for another); a host row with `browser` is a chat app open in the person's own signed-in browser, woken by harness/tell-a-chat-app.mjs, which types `message` into that chat and sends it: `routes` are the ways to reach the person's browser, tried in order: `{ kind: "cdp", cdp }` a debugging address (a browser started with --remote-debugging-port), or `{ kind: "apple-events", app, refused }` the named browser app's own AppleScript `execute javascript` in a new tab, with `refused` rows (`contains`: words of the refusal, `say`: the plain words naming the setting to turn on), `open` the chat's address with {session} and `open_new` a new chat's, and `composer`, `send` (`buttons`, else `key`) and `signed_out` are selectors tried in order, `read_on` the day they were read from the live page and `read_from` where; `live_check` (optional) lists the host's running sessions as JSON and `live_path` the field holding each session's id, so a session that is already running elsewhere is never started a second time; `when_live` says what to do then (`skip`: leave the work for that running session to be told another way). `message` is the words the started AI reads, with {handoff_id}, {agent_id} and {job}. A new host is one row here; the consumer names none.
message: Trillion handed work {handoff_id} to you as agent {agent_id}: "{job}". Read it with read_handoff, take it with take_work (agent_id "{agent_id}", handoff_id "{handoff_id}"), do it, then finish_work with the result. This notice comes from Trillion, not from the person.

refused.say: macOS did not let this program control Arc: in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation, allow the app running Trillion's helper (Terminal or your AI app) to control Arc
Google Chrome does not run JavaScript sent by other programs: in Chrome's menu bar choose View, Developer, Allow JavaScript from Apple Events
macOS did not let this program control Google Chrome: in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation, allow the app running Trillion's helper (Terminal or your AI app) to control Google Chrome

browser.read_from: a signed-in chatgpt.com page in a desktop browser, read-only on 2026-09-30 (nothing typed or sent): the message box is div.ProseMirror[contenteditable=true][role=textbox] (aria-label Ask ChatGPT, no #prompt-textarea), no sign-in buttons; the send button is not on the page until text is in the box, so its selectors are the signed-out page's (button[data-composer-submit]) and the older data-testid, with Enter when neither appears. textarea[name=prompt] and [data-login-button] are from the signed-out page the same day
